title: Week 31 Mastery Quiz · Technology, AI, Surveillance, and Digital Rights

questions.question: UDHR Article 12 addresses privacy interests. A fictional agency claims consent to one service authorizes all future data sharing. What issue arises?
options: All public-sector uses are identical.
A privacy statement automatically prevents misuse.
Any consent permanently removes privacy interests.
Purpose limitation, meaningful consent, legal authority and downstream privacy risks require separate examination.
questions.explanation: Purpose limitation, meaningful consent, legal authority and downstream privacy risks require separate examination.

questions.question: A benefit-screening algorithm flags 90 of 100 ineligible applicants and incorrectly flags 30 eligible applicants. Which further metric best assesses equity?
options: Compare false-positive rates by group using appropriate group-specific denominators.
Only report the 90 detected cases.
Treat all flagged applicants as ineligible.
Measure fairness exclusively by software cost.
questions.explanation: Compare false-positive rates by group using appropriate group-specific denominators.

questions.question: A facial-recognition pilot publishes a single overall accuracy score without subgroup results. What limitation matters?
options: An average proves equal performance for every person.
Aggregate performance can conceal uneven error rates across subpopulations and deployment settings.
Group-level review is impossible.
The system's accuracy is independent of context.
questions.explanation: Aggregate performance can conceal uneven error rates across subpopulations and deployment settings.

questions.question: A fictional state deploys automated surveillance with no appeal or independent review. What institutional safeguard is missing?
options: Only greater server capacity.
A longer marketing description.
Effective challenge procedures, oversight, transparency and lawful limits on collection and use.
A policy allowing indefinite retention.
questions.explanation: Effective challenge procedures, oversight, transparency and lawful limits on collection and use.

questions.question: Two AI vendors report 95% and 98% accuracy on different test sets. What comparative conclusion is justified?
options: 98% always means better public outcomes.
Test-set composition cannot affect accuracy.
The vendors have identical error costs.
Neither score establishes superiority without comparable populations, labels, tasks and conditions.
questions.explanation: Neither score establishes superiority without comparable populations, labels, tasks and conditions.

questions.question: An education algorithm predicts dropout risk using postal codes. What should a senior investigate before deployment?
options: Proxy discrimination, data validity, interventions offered and mechanisms for correction.
Only the number of training rows.
Whether the model name sounds impartial.
Assume postal codes represent educational ability.
questions.explanation: Proxy discrimination, data validity, interventions offered and mechanisms for correction.

questions.question: A public service chatbot generates fabricated citations in a legal explanation. Which evidence protocol is required?
options: Treat fluent text as legal evidence.
Verify cited authority, link each claim to actual provisions and provide correction or escalation paths.
Remove links so errors cannot be checked.
Use the chatbot's confidence wording as proof.
questions.explanation: Verify cited authority, link each claim to actual provisions and provide correction or escalation paths.

questions.question: A ministry retains biometric records indefinitely despite no stated operational need. What governance question is central?
options: Whether storage is inexpensive.
Whether the agency has enough servers.
Necessity, lawful basis, retention limits, security and independent accountability.
Assume unlimited storage is a legal right.
questions.explanation: Necessity, lawful basis, retention limits, security and independent accountability.

questions.question: A platform claims neutral content ranking but refuses to explain its moderation appeal process. What should analysts distinguish?
options: A neutral branding claim proves fair enforcement.
Appeals are unrelated to expression.
Transparency requires publicizing every private user record.
Ranking methods, governance rules, rights implications and practical access to redress.
questions.explanation: Ranking methods, governance rules, rights implications and practical access to redress.

questions.question: A senior argues Article 19 guarantees algorithmic promotion of every message. What interpretation is more defensible?
options: Analyze the protection of expression separately from claims about platform amplification, applicable law and competing rights.
Every private platform must amplify all content equally.
The article gives a guaranteed algorithmic ranking.
Expressive rights eliminate platform safety responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Analyze the protection of expression separately from claims about platform amplification, applicable law and competing rights.

shortResponse: How should law and democratic governance respond when digital systems redistribute information, power, labor, privacy, and risk?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
